description: Rick returns to Cornwall through the places and people that shaped him, combining seafood and farming with art, mining, religion, folklore and family memory to show a county much stranger and richer than its holiday image.

s11e01.description: Rick returns to the Trevose Head coast where he grew up, revisiting childhood fishing with his father and the family memories that made Cornwall and the sea central to his life.

s11e02.description: A family making Gouda-style cheese leads to Mevagissey's pilchard history and sea-shanty tradition, before Rick cooks a tortilla with caramelised apples and onions.

s11e03.description: At Combeshead Farm, Rick follows a field-to-fork approach built around Mangalitsa pigs and cooks pork chops with sloe berries, then joins his son Jack for a clam bake beside the Camel Estuary.

s11e04.description: Launceston's Norman castle and local superstitions begin a journey west, where composers Graham Fitkin and Ruth Wall connect Cornwall's landscape with an equally distinctive musical culture.

s11e05.description: Rick fishes for crab, walks with Barry Humphries through country loved by John Betjeman and meets Perranporth's cold-water Bluetits, turning the catch into a Cornish crab omelette.

s11e06.description: The Camel Valley grape harvest shows how Cornwall became credible wine country, while fishing for fast-moving mackerel leads to a Goa-inspired barbecue and a conversation with Tim Smit about the origins of the Eden Project.

s11e07.description: Around the Fowey Estuary, Rick mixes stories of piracy with crab Scotch eggs, Cornish vodka and a blackberry-and-clotted-cream pancake, finding local reinvention beside old maritime history.

s11e08.description: Nathan Outlaw joins Rick for lobster fishing and a discussion of conservation before a lobster risotto, while Tresillian's walled garden experiments with harvesting by lunar cycles and supplies vegetables for a Cornish briam.

s11e09.description: A walk with Dawn French at Golitha Falls gives way to the Tamar's chain ferry and its improbable circus-elephant story, before Rick uses a local 'superfood' in a duck dish.

s11e10.description: The vast china-clay pits explain Cornwall's 'white gold' and its artificial Alps; Rick then finds a hidden cove for a swim, cooks sea bass with homemade mayonnaise and visits his artist niece.

s11e11.description: St Ives' post-war modern-art community leads Rick toward the Lizard, where he fishes for red mullet and considers how the county's coast, food and symbols became inseparable from its modern identity.

s11e12.description: On the Roseland Peninsula, Rick encounters an old Jerusalem tradition, visits St Mawes with Alex and Olga Polizzi and explores aged meat, steak with béarnaise and the work of a Mousehole potter.

s11e13.description: Tintagel's King Arthur legends contrast with Camborne's Methodist history and feast-bun tradition, while a local family reviving saffron cultivation gives Rick the essential ingredient for Cornish saffron buns.

s11e14.description: Rick follows the rugged West Penwith coast through Lamorna and the old tin and copper workings around Botallack, searches for traces of Cornwall's oldest buildings and recalls the bouillabaisse that first changed his idea of seafood.

s11e15.description: A Truro ghost story and cathedral visit lead to a family devoted to offal and a meal of pickled ox tongue and beef-heart tacos, before Rick visits Hawker's Hut and the graves of sailors recovered from shipwrecks.
